tip: After говорите (gavarite = you speak), a language takes the по- adverb: по-английски (pa-angliyski), по-русски (pa-russki), not the noun form.
'By' a vehicle uses на (na) plus the prepositional: на велосипеде (na velasipede = by bicycle). Same на (na) as 'on', different job.
помогать (pamagat' = to help) takes a dative object with no 'to': помогает младшему (pamagaet mladshemu = helps the younger one), with the -ему (-emu) ending.
The pair ни...ни (ni...ni = neither...nor) still needs не (ne) on the verb: не хочу (ne khachu = I don't want). Russian keeps both negatives.
After с (s = with), the noun goes instrumental: с которой (s katoray = with whom). которой is the instrumental of который (katoryy = which).
The word откуда (atkuda = from where) asks origin, unlike где (gde = where) for location and куда (kuda = where to) for destination.
'Than anyone' after a comparative is just the genitive: усерднее всех (userdneye vsekh = harder than everyone). Here no separate 'than' word is needed.
зовут (zavut = they call) is a subjectless they-form, so как вас зовут (kak vas zavut) is literally how they call you.
The frame по (po) plus a -ски (-ski) ending means in a language: по-английски (pa-angliyski = in English), always one lowercase word.
написал (napisal) is perfective, presenting the writing as one finished act: кто написал (kto napisal = who wrote) this book.
After numbers five and up the counted noun usually goes genitive plural: пятнадцать процентов (pyatnadtsat pratsentav = fifteen percent).
Seasons take the instrumental to mean in that season: весной (vesnoy = in spring), with no preposition.
The word неужели (neuzheli) opens a question of disbelief, meaning really or you cannot be serious: неужели он уже уехал (neuzheli on uzhe uekhal).
Possession puts the owner in genitive after the thing owned: дом моего брата (dom maevo brata = my brother's house).
Feminine nouns in -а (a) shift to -у (u) as a direct object: читает книгу (chitaet knigu = reads a book).
The -ся (-sya) on отправляется (atpravlyaetsya = departs) makes the verb act on itself, so it takes no object.
до (do = up to) takes the genitive: до конца (do kantsa = to the end).
давай (davay = let us) plus a we-form verb makes a suggestion: давай встретимся (davay vstretimsya = let's meet).
о (o = about) takes the prepositional case: о древней истории (o drevney istorii = about ancient history).
Negated existence forces the genitive: нет свободных мест (net svabodnykh mest = there are no free seats).
Russian usually has no verb to have, it uses у (u) plus genitive: у друга есть (u druga est = the friend has).
на (na = on) takes the prepositional case for location: на столе (na stale = on the table). The base form стол (stol) shifts to столе.
Imperfective future is буду/будешь (budu/budesh) plus an infinitive; the verb itself does not change: буду есть (budu yest = will eat).
нет (net = there isn't) forces genitive: ничего невозможного (nichevo nevazmozhnava = nothing impossible), not a nominative form.
The word откуда (atkuda = from where) asks where motion starts, куда (kuda = where to) asks the destination. Both go with motion verbs.
картой (kartay = by card) is instrumental: paying by means of something uses the instrumental form with no preposition. Base карта (karta) becomes картой.
The frame что это за (shto eta za = what kind of) keeps the noun nominative: что это за здание (zdanie = building), not a genitive form.
по-русски (pa-russki = in Russian) is an adverb, not a noun. Use it with говорю (gavaryu = speak): say говорю по-русски, not говорю русский.
ничего (nichevo = nothing) still needs не (ne = not) on the verb: ничего не понимаю (ne panimayu = don't understand). Russian keeps both negatives.
домой (damoy = homeward) marks motion toward home. Being at home would be дома (doma = at home). Different words for going versus being.
